subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a load-time repair that deletes only dead-end same-parent compaction retry entries from persisted session JSONL, or require write-side retry prevention before repairing existing files?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not whether the report is plausible; it is whether removing structurally valid but semantically superseded persisted session entries is an acceptable recovery policy.

options.title: Approve narrow repair and refresh PR
options.body: Accept the compaction-only deletion rule, refresh the linked PR over current main, integrate the incremental repair cache path, and land focused regression coverage.

options.title: Require write-side prevention first
options.body: Pause the repair until compaction retry writes become idempotent or otherwise unable to create same-parent compaction siblings.

options.title: Split repair and prevention
options.body: Land an explicitly approved existing-file repair now and track source-side duplicate prevention as separate follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow repair and refresh PR
recommendation.body: Accept the compaction-only deletion rule, refresh the linked PR over current main, integrate the incremental repair cache path, and land focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent session repair cache work is the current code path the candidate fix must fit before the policy can land safely.
